note: Wiring harnesses for the Board Room's Wire-it view. HONESTY CONTRACT: `to` pin names must exist in the board's pads/pinout in devices/boards.json (drift-gated there against firmware configs + BOM); per-connection `status` mirrors the pinout row's status — a `planned` wire is defined in firmware config but not yet driven/read by the current build. Peripheral shapes are procedural stand-ins sized from their datasheets (schematic, not vendor CAD); wire ROUTING is staged for legibility — only the endpoints are claims. `signal`/`dir` name the firmware-facing signal each wire carries: that is the future binding point for live pin emulation (the wasm emulator's GPIO bus lighting these same pins), so they must match the feature names the firmware configs use. Builds are data, not code: a device may carry any number of builds (permutations — field vs bedside vs battery-less), and tests/boardroom.test.js validates every reference.

piezo.name: Passive piezo disc
piezo.blurb: Passive element — it only sounds when the firmware drives it (LEDC PWM); no onboard oscillator.

reed.name: Reed switch
reed.blurb: Glass-tube reed, no polarity. Closes near the enclosure magnet; firmware reads it active-low with the internal pull-up — no external resistor.

ws2812.name: WS2812 status LED
ws2812.blurb: One addressable RGB pixel. Data flows one way — wire DIN, not DOUT, to the board.

gnss_l76k.name: L76K GNSS module
gnss_l76k.blurb: UART GNSS with ceramic patch antenna, 9600 baud. TX and RX cross: the module talks out of TX into the board's RX.

vbat_divider.name: VBAT divider (2:1)
vbat_divider.blurb: Two equal resistors halve the battery voltage so the 3.3 V ADC can read a 4.2 V cell — VBAT_DIVIDER_RATIO=2.0 undoes the halving in firmware.

lipo.name: LiPo cell
lipo.blurb: Single-cell LiPo on the board's battery pads; the XIAO's onboard charger manages it. Polarity is not survivable — check twice.

builds.title: WAP field build — chirp, tamper, GNSS, battery
builds.note: The full off-grid loadout from the WAP BOM: every wire below lands on the exact castellated pad the firmware config names. Power (the battery) connects LAST — build practice the step order enforces.

steps.title: Chirp buzzer
steps.note: Two wires. The piezo is passive — the LEDC PWM on D1 is what makes the sound, so a mixed-up pin stays silent, not broken.

steps.title: Tamper reed
steps.note: No polarity: either leg to D3, the other to GND. The internal pull-up holds the pin high; the enclosure magnet closing the reed pulls it low.

steps.title: GNSS module
steps.note: The classic crossover: module TX → board D7 (RX), module RX → board D6 (TX). Straight-through wiring is the #1 'my GPS is dead' cause.

steps.title: Status LED
steps.note: Data in on DIN only — DOUT is for chaining more pixels away from the board.

steps.title: VBAT sense divider
steps.note: The divider's midpoint goes to A0; firmware multiplies by 2.0 to recover the real cell voltage.

steps.title: Battery — last
steps.note: Power connects last, after every signal wire is seated and checked. BAT pads are on the board's underside; polarity is not survivable.

builds.title: Watch Station — the one wire: the battery
builds.note: The watch is a zero-wire stack: the plain XIAO seats in the Round Display's XIAO socket and gets display SPI, backlight, touch, RTC and microSD through the socket with no jumpers. The only harness is the protected 150 mAh LiPo into the display's own JST 1.25 charger input — so this "wire it" is deliberately just that one connector. Polarity is not survivable; the display silk, not the cell's wire colour, is ground truth.

steps.title: Battery into the JST
steps.note: The 302030 protected cell plugs into the Round Display's JST 1.25. The onboard charger tops it off over USB-C; the XIAO reads pack voltage through the socket. Check polarity against the display silk before it clicks home.

connections.note: cell + into the display's charger JST (verify polarity on the silk)
